summary.decision: Stand aside for both long-term buying and swing trades. All three readings still point the same way.

note.headline: Tesla flat at 384.68 as a SpaceX merger is reported; still avoid

summary.thesis: Sales have stalled and margins and cash flow are shrinking, while the price sits near the top of Tesla's own valuation history, so the reported SpaceX merger talk changes the story but not the numbers.
summary.decision: Long-term avoid; swing wait until the price leaves the 363.93–404.4 band.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94; swing only on a close above 404.4 or a hold of 363.93–368.69

note.happening: Tesla closed at 384.68, down 0.2%. That holds most of yesterday's jump and sits inside the 380.15–389.95 zone, just under resistance at 393.63–404.4. The Financial Times reported that directors are negotiating a SpaceX-Tesla merger, called the biggest ever. No filing confirms it. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
note.business: The merger report is about governance and sentiment, not about how many cars Tesla sells or what it earns on each one. Until terms are filed, it changes nothing in the reported numbers. SpaceX is a private rocket and satellite company with the same CEO (general knowledge), so a deal would raise questions about who gets what price and whether outside shareholders are treated fairly (general knowledge). The business picture itself is weak. Sales in the latest quarter fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin slipped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Inventory rose 15% while sales were flat, and unsold cars can lead to price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. The balance sheet is not at risk: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity mean the company can fund itself. What is at risk is profit: margins and cash generation are going the wrong way.

worth.text: At 384.68, Tesla is worth about 1521.0B. That is 423.3 times trailing earnings and 14.7 times sales. Its price-to-sales ratio is higher than 77.0% of its own last five years. A cash-flow model (DCF) built on the 3.3B of free cash flow gives 20.01 to 44.3 per share, with a base of 24.66. Even if sales started growing 30% a year, that model gives only 45.31. Comparing the price with Tesla's own price-to-sales history gives 203.8 at the low end, 293.94 in the middle and 399.81 at the top. The gap between the two methods comes from one assumption: whether you value Tesla on the cash it makes today or on the high multiple the market has paid for its future before. The filings note that the price needs about 50% a year growth, while Tesla has delivered 3% a year over three years. I use the own-history range, because the DCF ignores what the market has actually paid for this stock. Even so, the price is above the middle of that range.
worth.key_assumption: With flat sales and shrinking margins, the market values Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity, so there is no funding risk.
Trailing revenue still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 25%.
Options traders hold the most open contracts in the 400 call (15193), and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.77, so positioning leans toward upside.
bear: Latest-quarter sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, and operating margin dropped to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Trailing free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, while inventory rose 15% against flat sales.
The price is 423.3 times earnings and above every DCF value (base 24.66, bull 44.3). The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.66, so there is no value support here.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.93–368.69), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it would end the rebound and point toward 349.31–354.07.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all falling, and the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The merger report adds governance uncertainty but no business improvement.

swing.why: The price sits between support at 363.93–368.69 and resistance at 393.63–404.4 (touched 5 times), the trend is marked as down, and all three averages are flat, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or a pullback that holds 363.93–368.69.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price a 10.7% move by 2026-12-18 and a 19.0% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report. Recent actual swings (72.9) have been larger than what options imply (51.5), and any filed merger terms could move the price before earnings.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago. That would make me reconsider, starting near 293.94.
A daily close above 404.4, the top of the resistance zone touched 5 times, would break the range and allow a swing entry.
A filed merger agreement whose terms are published. That would turn the report into a confirmed event, and the valuation would need to be redone on those terms.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid; the price held at 384.68 inside the 380.15–389.95 zone and under resistance at 393.63–404.4, and the reported SpaceX merger talk added no change to the shrinking margins or cash flow.

note.headline: NVIDIA drops 5.86% to 155.38 as Huang comeback rally fades; still hold

summary.thesis: NVIDIA's cash generation is exceptional, and today's price already assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 20% a year. The upside depends on a record 65% operating margin holding.
summary.decision: Hold the long-term position and make no swing trade while the price sits between support and resistance in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Buy at 116.97, move to wait on a close below 147.14, trim near 222.58

note.happening: NVIDIA fell 5.86% to 155.38, giving back part of the rally that followed Jensen Huang's reported return as CEO. Headlines today are mostly about governance: the government's role in his return, open investigations, and a reported addition of Megaspeed to the U.S. trade blacklist over export controls. Our data has no earnings date, and the latest filed quarter ended 2026-07-26.
note.business: The business numbers are strong. Over the last twelve months revenue was 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 127.0B, up from 72.0B. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and the company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. None of today's CEO news changes these figures. The leadership drama, the investigations and Huang reportedly saying he still does not believe in succession planning affect sentiment and governance, not demand. Two items could touch the business. First, the Megaspeed blacklisting (reported) concerns export controls, which can limit where chips are sold (general knowledge). Second, Amazon's reported Decart deal is a bet on narrowing the chip gap with NVIDIA, a long-run competition risk. The real risks come from the filings. The 65% margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, and peaks like that usually fade. Money customers still owe is up 127% while quarterly sales are up 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Demand itself does not look at risk today. What is at risk is how long the margin and the payment timing hold.

worth.text: The two methods disagree mainly because they make different assumptions about growth. A discounted cash flow model values the company from its expected future cash. Using the 127.0B in trailing free cash flow and a discount rate near 10%, it gives 191.49 (bear), 222.58 (base) and 264.22 (bull). The company's own price-to-sales history gives 217.35 to 411.04. The more useful reading runs the other way. At 155.38, the price matches the model value of 155.64, which is what 20% starting growth produces, and the data puts the implied starting growth at 20.0%. So the market is not paying for the 83% sales growth of last year. It is paying for growth to slow sharply. The biggest swing factor is margin. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 116.97, and at 32% it drops to 78.3. The data's valuation summary quotes an older price of 165.05, so today's price sits even lower against those ranges. Multiples tell the same story: 19.6 times trailing earnings, 9.4 times next year's expected earnings, and 12.4 times sales against a peer median of 14.9.
worth.key_assumption: Operating margin stays near 65.21% rather than fading toward 48%, while free cash flow grows from 127.0B at a starting rate of about 20% or more.

bull: The stock trades at 9.4 times analysts' next-year earnings estimate, and that estimate has risen 27.7% over 90 days.
Free cash flow reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B, with 23.2B more cash than debt.
Price-to-sales of 12.4 is below the peer median of 14.9 and sits at the 9th percentile of NVIDIA's own 5-year range.
bear: Operating margin of 65% is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, and a fade to 48% would put model value at 116.97.
Money customers owe is up 127% against sales up 106%, which can be a sign of pulled-forward sales or stretched customers.
The trend is down, and the price sits well below the 50-day average of 204.95 and the falling 20-day average of 175.78.

levels.what: Bottom of the only support zone (147.14–150.46). A close below it moves the call to wait.
Model value if operating margin falls to 48%. Buy at 116.97, because that price already allows for a large margin fade.
Base-case cash-flow value. Trim near it, because at that price the market would be paying for the full current margin and growth.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the committee says 'Hold'. The price already assumes about 20% growth and relies on a peak margin, and the slow-payment risk is unresolved, so the call is hold rather than add.

swing.why: The price sits between support at 147.14–150.46 and resistance at 163.9–171.33 (4 touches), in a downtrend. A typical day's range is 13.32, which would blow through a tight stop. No trade until the price holds the 147.14–150.46 zone or closes above 171.33.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date. The next quarterly filing will show whether the 65.21% margin and customer payments hold. The options data is from 2026-11-23 and priced off 165.05, so its expected moves are out of date after today's drop.

change_mind: A close below 147.14 would break the only support zone and move the long-term call from hold to wait.
If the next filing shows operating margin falling back toward 58.09%, or the gap between money owed (up 127%) and sales (up 106%) widening, the fair-value view moves toward 116.97.
A close above 171.33, the top of the 4-touch resistance zone, would turn the swing call from wait to enter.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: hold, confirmed by the price falling to 155.38, which matches the 155.64 value implied by 20% starting growth (the margin-fade value at 48% is now 116.97, up from 114.82).
note.label: Research, not advice.

note.headline: AMD falls 8.86% to 413.27, still well above every fair-value estimate

summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade while the stock is in a downtrend and below its 200-day average.

worth.text: At 413.27 AMD trades at 90.1 times trailing earnings, 51.1 times this year's expected earnings and 23.4 times next year's. note.headline: Amazon slips 1.21% to 252.29; cash burn keeps us waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Amazon keeps growing and its margins are improving, but it is spending more cash than it brings in, and the price already sits near the top of its usual value range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price stays in a downtrend between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Buy at 238.65; small buy at 245.59 only after better cash flow; no buying above 265.96

note.happening: Amazon closed at 252.29, down 1.21% on the day. The stock is in a downtrend. It trades below its 20-day average of 257.7 and its 50-day average of 255.15, but still above its 200-day average of 245.59. Amazon was reported to be buying Decart to help close its AI-chip gap with Nvidia, and the FAA was reported to be probing a delivery-drone accident. The next earnings report is due 2027-02-04.
note.business: Sales are still growing, but more slowly. Quarterly sales rose 12.09% from a year earlier, down from 16.61% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the profit kept from each dollar of sales before interest and tax, improved to 13.09% from 11.02%. The weak spot is cash. Free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and paying for new buildings and equipment, was -46.9B over the last 12 months, against 10.6B a year earlier. Debt exceeds cash by 66.7B. Even so, 114.2B of liquidity (cash plus credit it can draw on) means there is no near-term funding risk. The filings also flag two things: unpaid customer bills grew 61% while sales grew 12%, and the 13% operating margin sits at the top of its 5-year range of 2–13%. Today's news changes little in the business. The reported Decart deal is a strategic bet on AI chips that could matter over the long run, but it does not change current demand or margins. The reported FAA drone probe is a regulatory and sentiment issue, not a hit to earnings. The Apple TV discount is minor. What is at risk is how much cash Amazon generates and how long its margin stays at the peak. Demand itself is not at risk: sales over the last 12 months reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value, a method that values a company by its future cash, because free cash flow is negative. That leaves the company's own price-to-sales history. Price-to-sales is the stock price divided by sales per share. Over 5 years, that history gives a fair-value range of 187.93 to 265.96, with a middle of 238.65. At 252.29 the stock is above the middle and below the top. Its price-to-sales of 3.4 sits at the 67th percentile of its own 5-year history, which means it has been cheaper about two-thirds of the time. Against peers it looks cheap: the peer median is 6.4, and on a growth-adjusted basis it trades at 0.62 of what peers trade at. The stock costs 20.5 times trailing earnings and 19.7 times this year's expected earnings. On next year's expected earnings the multiple rises to 23.6, because analysts expect earnings per share to fall from 12.8 to 10.67. The filings estimate that the price needs about 33% yearly growth, while the company delivered 13% a year over the last 3 years. Most of the gap between methods comes from one choice: whether Amazon should be valued against its own past or against its peers.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.4.

bull: Price-to-sales of 3.4 is well below the peer median of 6.4, and growth-adjusted value is 0.62 of peers.
Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now keeps more profit.
Sales over the last 12 months grew to 797.5B from 691.3B, and analysts expect 959.6B next year.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from 10.6B, and debt exceeds cash by 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, and unpaid customer bills grew 61%.
Analysts expect earnings per share to fall from 12.8 this year to 10.67 next year, which lifts the forward multiple to 23.6.

levels.what: The middle of the own-history value range, inside the 232.99–238.97 support zone (a price area where buyers have stepped in before). This is the main buy level.
The 200-day average, inside the strong 244.3–249.71 support zone (9 touches). A small first buy here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.

longterm.why: The price of 58.87 is below the DCF base of 63.7, the own-history low of 58.94 and the 59.9 margin-fade value. Estimates are still being trimmed and no support level is listed, so adds stay small and staggered.

swing.why: The trend is down, the price is under every falling average, and resistance sits at 61.14–61.64 and 64.56–65.08. No support level gives a place for a stop, and put open interest is 3.03 times call open interest, so no trade until a close above 65.08.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report falls before the 2027-02-19 option expiry, which prices a move of about 17.1%. So adds stop at the 53.74 slice before the report, and further buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-19 report shows operating margin below 23%, the value falls under 59.9 and the move would be to wait, not add.
If next-year EPS consensus drops below 3.56, today's lowest analyst estimate, the 12.2% implied growth looks too high and adds would pause.
A close above 65.08 would break the resistance ceiling and reopen a swing entry.
